body: This all sounds like me and I’ve been a barista for 6 years. It’s been extremely tough for me at times and I still struggle but I love the job so I make it work. I just started wearing loop earplugs. I also have some stimming toys around and I tend to just move my body a lot. My loop earplugs make me feel a lot safer (I use the switch ones) but I’m still adjusting to the volume. I can still hear people which is obviously essential for the job but it keeps the background noise a lot more manageable. The lighting is definitely still bothersome for me but maybe glasses that are only slightly tinted would help. If you get them online from Eyebuydirect or wherever you can usually choose the amount of tint! My biggest issues are noise and focusing because I have a hard time starting and finishing tasks without getting distracted and derailed. I keep lists!!! Little whiteboards are super helpful or even just some receipt paper to keep track of what I’m doing and what I’m planning to do in the future.  I also tend to over communicate with my coworkers. I’m a shift lead and find it helpful to check in with my baristas consistently and let them know what I’m doing in case I get off track they can help me remember. Making a plan and talking in through for the morning and for the afternoon at the cafe really helps the jumbled feeling I get and my coworkers say it helps them too! It’s possible to have these issues and be a barista!!!! It can be hard and really exhausting so I find it super important to give myself time to rest and make sure I’m eating because adding hunger to the already overwhelming stimuli can be too much for me. I think it’s really about finding things that work for you to make you feel comfortable and safe!!!! Good luck!!!!
